claims: C1: Models should honor user requests.
C2: The obligation to honor a user request is withdrawn when that request conflicts with a developer-, system-, or root-level instruction.

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: the level of instruction authority held by instructions from end users

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels, ordered from higher to lower: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority

concepts.name: user_request
concepts.gloss: R is a request made by an end user
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of 'user requests', so a class of requests made by end users is presupposed

concepts.name: higher_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction at the developer, system, or root level of the authority hierarchy

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: request R and instruction I direct incompatible behavior, so that honoring R would violate I
concepts.inference: the clause's 'unless they conflict' requires a relation between a request and an instruction that makes them incompatible

ontology.gloss: I is an instruction at the developer, system, or root level of the authority hierarchy

asserts.read_back: honoring user request % is obliged unless it conflicts with a developer-, system-, or root-level instruction
asserts.body: user_request(R), not higher_level_instruction(I), not conflicts_with(R, I)

closure.reason: The clause states an obligation to honor user requests and withdraws it only when a conflict with a higher-level instruction exists; it takes no position on requests that are not user requests or on other acts, so silence on those is unsettled by this clause.
